target_customer: DevOps, site reliability and IT operations teams at software companies and enterprises
problem: Engineers carried pagers and relied on noisy email alerts and ad hoc scripts to be woken up for outages. PagerDuty routes alerts, schedules on call rotations and manages incidents.
business_model: B2B SaaS per user subscription with tiers, plus add on products

founders.name: Alex Solomon
founders.background_notes: Pushed the first commit on 2009-02-18 and carried a pager at Amazon. Served as CTO until 2020 and GM of Platform until 2024 per the YC page.

founders.name: Andrew Miklas
founders.background_notes: Met the other founders at Amazon where they carried pagers.

founders.name: Baskar Puvanathasan
founders.background_notes: Met the other founders at Amazon where they carried pagers.

technical_complexity.rationale: Reliable alert delivery by phone, SMS and push with high uptime was a hard operational problem for a tiny team even though the logic was simple.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations with monitoring tools and on call schedules embedded in team workflows created switching costs; reliability reputation mattered for a tool that must not fail.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Competitors OpsGenie and VictorOps emerged and were acquired by Atlassian and Splunk later. PagerDuty remained independent and went public in April 2019.

market_need_then: Cloud adoption in 2009 and 2010 pushed engineers to run always on services and be on call. The founders felt the pain at Amazon, and the first beta launched on Hacker News in August 2009.

branding.name_origin: Name tied to the on call duty carried by pager; a PagerDuty interview discusses the naming but details were not retrieved.

identity.logo: Green wordmark; the company says its name, logo and PagerDuty Green remain the core of its identity system
identity.visual_style: Signature PagerDuty Green with the Volt accent added in a 2023 refresh
identity.voice_and_tone: Operations and reliability focused; recent taglines include Operations in the AI Era

rebrands.why: Brand refresh keeping name, logo and green; details not retrieved

branding.community_and_virality: Brand guidelines restrict use of marks on merchandise; no fan community evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: The name is descriptive of the product and the green identity is distinctive, though sources found for brand impact are limited to the company's own pages.

outcome_analysis: PagerDuty grew from founders who carried pagers at Amazon, launching in 2009 and joining YC in 2010. Funded by Andreessen Horowitz, Bessemer, Accel and others, it reached a reported 1.3 billion dollar valuation in 2018 and IPO'd on the NYSE in April 2019 at 24 dollars a share, raising about 218 million dollars at roughly a 1.8 billion dollar valuation. Founder market fit, integrations and cloud adoption drove the success.
notes: Series B and Series D amounts come from aggregators (Clay, StartupIntros, CB Insights) and should be treated as unverified in detail; series C of about 43.8 million dollars in April 2017 led by Accel appears only on Clay and is not listed. A 350 million dollar convertible note in October 2023 appeared on a single aggregator and is not listed. No dated 2009 to 2010 competitor sources were found, so the list is empty; OpsGenie and VictorOps were not confirmed by sources. The IPO row is recorded as growth with IPO proceeds. Employee reductions in 2024 were not verified. The Andy Billinghurst founder claim on a wiki page was ignored.
